newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia seeks Colombian help on East Timor.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia seeks Colombian help on East Timor.

text.p: Indonesia sought the help of Colombia on Thursday to keep the controversial East Timor issue off the agenda at a summit meeting of Latin American nations, Spain and Portugal due to be held in Chile next month.
Indonesia's State Secretary Murdiono told reporters that President Suharto had asked the visiting Colombian President Ernesto Samper to help prevent Portugal raising the issue.
"There are strong signs that Portugal will bring the East Timor issue to the IBOR-American forum," Murdiono said following talks between the two presidents.

Portugal, the former colonial ruler of East Timor until 1975, has been pressing for a U.N.-sponsored referendum on the future of the territory which Indonesia incorporated as its 27th province in 1976.
The IBOR-American forum will bring together the leaders of Latin American countries, Spain and Portugal.
Murdiono said that in his talks with Samper, Suharto had "stressed that there is already a forum to deal with the East Timor issue and it should not be dealt with at an international gathering".
The state secretary said Samper had said Colombia would "pay serious attention to Indonesia's views on the issue".

Indonesia and Portugal have held a series of meetings on the issue under the auspices of the United Nations, but have failed so far to reach agreement. The United Nations has refused to recognise Indonesian sovereignty over the territory and regards Portugal as the administering power.
Indonesian troops moved into East Timor in December 1975 and Jakarta says local tribal chiefs requested integration into Indonesia the following year.
Murdiono said the two presidents agreed to coordinate policy over the future of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM), which Colombia currently heads.
He said Suharto and Samper also agreed to increase trade and expand economic relations. Indonesia's Industry and Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo would visit Colombia next year, he added.
Samper left for South Korea on Thursday after a two-day visit to Indonesia.
